"""
Context managers for manual span creation.
"""

from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional, Union

from opentelemetry import trace as otel_trace

from ..errors import NeatlogsConfigurationError


def _reject_http_span_kind(kind: Any, attributes: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    candidates = (
        kind,
        attributes.get("neatlogs.span.kind"),
        attributes.get("openinference.span.kind"),
    )
    if any(str(value or "").strip().upper() == "HTTP" for value in candidates):
        raise NeatlogsConfigurationError(
            "HTTP spans are not supported. Trace the semantic LLM, TOOL, "
            "RETRIEVER, or other AI operation instead."
        )


@contextmanager
def trace(
    name: str,
    kind: Optional[str] = None,
    system_prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "SystemPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    system_prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    user_prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "UserPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    user_prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    prompt_template: Optional[Union[str, "SystemPromptTemplate"]] = None,
    prompt_variables: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    version: Optional[str] = None,
    capture_stdout: bool = False,
    mask: Optional[Callable] = None,
    session_id: Optional[str] = None,
    end_user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    end_user_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    **attributes,
):
    """
    Context manager for prompt tracking and session management.

    IMPORTANT: This is NOT required for basic tracing!
    - Framework code (LangChain, OpenAI, etc.) is auto-instrumented
    - Custom code should use @span(kind="...") decorator

    Use trace() ONLY for:
    1. Prompt template tracking (captures template + variables for versioning)
    2. Multi-turn session management (groups turns within a session)
    3. Grouping multiple top-level operations in main()

    **When NOT to use trace():**
    - Don't wrap a single @span(kind="WORKFLOW") call - it's already traced!
    - Don't use for custom functions - use @span(kind="...") decorator instead
    - Don't use just to "create a span" - auto-instrumentation handles that

    **Session-Aware Trace Creation:**
    - If `session_id` is set in init() AND no active parent span exists,
      this creates a NEW root trace (for multi-turn conversations).
    - Otherwise, creates a normal child span within the existing trace.

    Args:
        name: Span name
        kind: OpenInference span kind (rarely needed - auto-inferred)
        system_prompt_template: SystemPromptTemplate object for system prompt versioning
        system_prompt_variables: Dict of system prompt variables (legacy string templates only)
        user_prompt_template: UserPromptTemplate object for user/human prompt versioning
        user_prompt_variables: Dict of user prompt variables (legacy string templates only)
        prompt_template: Deprecated alias for ``system_prompt_template``. Kept for
            backward compat; new code should use ``system_prompt_template``.
        prompt_variables: Deprecated alias for ``system_prompt_variables``.
        version: Optional version identifier
        end_user_id: Identifier of the END-USER this trace belongs to — i.e. the
            user of your application, not the operator running the SDK. One
            end-user per trace; the backend rolls this up to the trace and its
            session for filtering/analytics. Distinct from init(user_id=...).
        end_user_metadata: Optional dict of arbitrary end-user fields
            (e.g. {"plan": "pro", "email": "a@b.com"}), stored as JSON on the trace.
        **attributes: Additional attributes to set on the span

    Examples:

        Use Case 1: Prompt template tracking (inside your function):

        >>> template = SystemPromptTemplate([{"role": "user", "content": "{{query}}"}])
        >>>
        >>> @span(kind="AGENT")
        >>> def my_agent(query: str):
        ...     with trace(name="prompt", system_prompt_template=template):
        ...         messages = template.compile(query=query)  # Compile ONCE
        ...         response = llm.create(messages=messages)   # No duplication!
        ...     return response

        Use Case 2: Multi-turn sessions:

        >>> neatlogs.init(api_key="...", session_id="user-123")
        >>>
        >>> with trace(name="turn_1"):  # New root trace (same session)
        ...     agent.run("Hello")
        >>>
        >>> with trace(name="turn_2"):  # New root trace (same session)
        ...     agent.run("Tell me more")

        Use Case 3: Grouping multiple operations in main:

        >>> def main():
        ...     with trace(name="pipeline"):  # Groups multiple steps
        ...         step1()  # @span(kind="CHAIN")
        ...         step2()  # @span(kind="CHAIN")
        ...         step3()  # @span(kind="AGENT")

        What NOT to do:

        >>> @span(kind="WORKFLOW")
        >>> def my_workflow():
        ...     pass
        >>>
        >>> # ❌ WRONG: Redundant wrapper!
        >>> with trace(name="main"):
        ...     my_workflow()  # Already traced by @span decorator
        >>>
        >>> # ✅ CORRECT: Just call it
        >>> my_workflow()
    """
    _reject_http_span_kind(kind, attributes)

    import json
    import logging

    from opentelemetry.context import Context, attach, detach, get_current, set_value

    from ..init import get_session_config
    from ..prompt.template import (
        PromptContext,
        SystemPromptTemplate,
        UserPromptContext,
        UserPromptTemplate,
    )
    from .end_user import apply_end_user_attributes
    from .session import apply_session_attributes

    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    # Resolve from the NEATLOGS provider (not the OTel global) so trace() spans
    # never export into a co-tenant's pipeline (e.g. the user's Langfuse provider)
    # in isolated mode.
    from .._wrap_utils import (
        _neatlogs_root_kwargs,
        _resolve_root_workflow_name,
        _should_auto_root,
        apply_wrap_context_attributes,
        attach_as_current,
    )
    from .._wrap_utils import detach as _nl_detach
    from .._wrap_utils import (
        get_internal_tracer,
    )

    tracer = get_internal_tracer(__name__)

    # Resolve canonical kwargs. `system_prompt_template` / `system_prompt_variables`
    # are the canonical names; `prompt_template` / `prompt_variables` are kept as
    # deprecated aliases for backward compat. If both are supplied, the canonical
    # (system_*) name wins.
    if system_prompt_template is not None:
        prompt_template = system_prompt_template
    if system_prompt_variables is not None:
        prompt_variables = system_prompt_variables

    from .identity import current_end_user_id, current_end_user_metadata, current_session_id

    session_config = get_session_config()
    user_id = session_config.get("user_id")
    # Identity resolution (per field): explicit per-call arg > identify() context.
    # init() no longer carries session/end-user identity.
    session_id = session_id or current_session_id()
    end_user_id = end_user_id or current_end_user_id()
    end_user_metadata = end_user_metadata or current_end_user_metadata()
    # Only a NEATLOGS span counts as an active trace to nest under. A foreign span
    # (a user's own OTel/Langfuse tracer active in-process) must not be treated as
    # a parent — nesting under it dangles our trace off a parent the backend never
    # receives (no root → never finalizes). _has_active_recording_parent() ignores
    # foreign spans; when only a foreign span is active we treat this as a root.
    from .._wrap_utils import _has_active_recording_parent

    is_in_active_trace = _has_active_recording_parent()

    template_string = None
    is_prompt_template_obj = False

    if prompt_template is not None:
        if isinstance(prompt_template, SystemPromptTemplate):
            is_prompt_template_obj = True
            template_string = str(prompt_template.template)
            logger.debug(
                f"[trace] Using SystemPromptTemplate object with variables: {prompt_template.variables}"
            )

"""Runtime configuration read from the environment (and `.env` when present)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

# Values already in the process environment win over `.env`.
load_dotenv(PROJECT_ROOT / ".env", override=False)

SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS = ("anthropic", "openrouter")
OPENROUTER_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"


class ConfigError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when required configuration is missing or invalid."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    provider: str
    model: str
    temperature: float = 0.0
    max_output_tokens: int = 1024
    history_window: int = 24


def load_settings() -> Settings:
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "anthropic").strip().lower() or "anthropic"
    if provider not in SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"LLM_PROVIDER must be one of {SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS}, got {provider!r}"
        )
    model = os.environ.get("VICTIM_MODEL", "").strip()
    if not model:
        raise ConfigError("VICTIM_MODEL must be set to the model id the agent should use")
    return Settings(
        provider=provider,
        model=model,
        history_window=int(os.environ.get("REFUNDDESK_HISTORY_WINDOW", "24")),
    )

"""Loading eval task definitions from ``evals/`` and ``evals/heldout/``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .checks import CHECKS
from .config import PROJECT_ROOT

EVALS_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "evals"
HELDOUT_DIR = EVALS_DIR / "heldout"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Task:
    id: str
    description: str
    turns: list[str]
    store: dict[str, Any]
    faults: list[dict[str, Any]]
    checks: list[dict[str, Any]]
    heldout: bool
    path: Path


def _from_file(path: Path, heldout: bool) -> Task:
    raw = json.loads(path.read_text())
    task = Task(
        id=raw["id"],
        description=raw["description"],
        turns=list(raw["turns"]),
        store=raw["store"],
        faults=list(raw.get("faults", [])),
        checks=list(raw["checks"]),
        heldout=heldout,
        path=path,
    )
    if task.id != path.stem:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: id {task.id!r} must match the file name")
    if not task.turns or not task.checks:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: a task needs at least one turn and one check")
    unknown = [c["check"] for c in task.checks if c["check"] not in CHECKS]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: unknown checks {unknown}")
    return task


def list_tasks(include_heldout: bool = True) -> list[Task]:
    tasks = [_from_file(p, False) for p in sorted(EVALS_DIR.glob("*.json"))]
    if include_heldout:
        tasks += [_from_file(p, True) for p in sorted(HELDOUT_DIR.glob("*.json"))]
    return tasks


def load_task(task_id: str) -> Task:
    for directory, heldout in ((EVALS_DIR, False), (HELDOUT_DIR, True)):
        path = directory / f"{task_id}.json"
        if path.exists():
            return _from_file(path, heldout)
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"no task named {task_id!r} in {EVALS_DIR} or {HELDOUT_DIR}")

"""Run one eval task: ``python -m refunddesk.eval --task <id> --seed <n>``.

Prints one JSON object: passed, cost, latency, tokens, trace_id (plus details).
Each run is exactly one neatlogs trace whose root WORKFLOW span carries the
harness metadata (CULPRIT_RUN_ID, COMMIT_SHA, TASK_ID, REPETITION).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

# neatlogs must be initialised before provider clients are created, so the
# tracing module is imported (and init_tracing called) before llm/agent run.
from . import tracing


def _trace_id(span: Any) -> str | None:
    try:
        ctx = span.get_span_context()
        return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x") if ctx.trace_id else None
    except Exception:
        return None


def run_task(task_id: str, seed: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from .tasks import load_task

    task = load_task(task_id)
    meta = tracing.run_metadata(task.id, seed)
    tracing.init_tracing(meta)

    import neatlogs

    from .agent import RefundDeskAgent
    from .checks import run_checks
    from .config import load_settings
    from .faults import FaultPlan
    from .llm import LLMClient
    from .store import JsonStore
    from .tools import ToolRuntime, activate

    settings = load_settings()
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"task_id": task.id, "seed": seed, "heldout": task.heldout}
    started = time.perf_counter()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=f"refunddesk-{task.id}-") as tmp:
        store = JsonStore.create(Path(tmp) / "store.json", task.store)
        runtime = ToolRuntime(store=store, faults=FaultPlan.from_task(task.id, seed, task.faults))
        token = activate(runtime)
        root_attrs = {
            "neatlogs.metadata": json.dumps(meta, sort_keys=True),
            "input.value": json.dumps({"task_id": task.id, "seed": seed, "turns": task.turns}),
            "input.mime_type": "application/json",
            **{f"neatlogs.workflow.{k}": v for k, v in meta.items()},
        }
        with neatlogs.trace(
            "refunddesk.run_task",
            kind="WORKFLOW",
            session_id=f"{meta['culprit_run_id']}:{task.id}",
            **root_attrs,
        ) as root:
            result["trace_id"] = _trace_id(root)
            agent = RefundDeskAgent(llm=LLMClient(settings), history_window=settings.history_window)
            replies = []
            error = None
            try:
                for turn in task.turns:
                    replies.append(agent.handle_turn(turn))
            except Exception as exc:  # the run fails; the error is reported, not hidden
                error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            final_state = store.load()
            checks = run_checks(task.checks, final_state, runtime.log)
            passed = error is None and all(c["passed"] for c in checks)
            root.set_attribute(
                "output.value",
                json.dumps({"passed": passed, "replies": replies, "error": error, "checks": checks}),
            )
            root.set_attribute("output.mime_type", "application/json")
        tool_log = runtime.log
    latency = time.perf_counter() - started

    responses = agent.responses
    in_tok = [r.input_tokens for r in responses]
    out_tok = [r.output_tokens for r in responses]
    costs = [r.cost_usd for r in responses]
    tokens = {
        "input": sum(in_tok) if all(t is not None for t in in_tok) else None,
        "output": sum(out_tok) if all(t is not None for t in out_tok) else None,
    }
    tokens["total"] = (
        tokens["input"] + tokens["output"] if None not in (tokens["input"], tokens["output"]) else None
    )
    result.update(

    d = {"order_id": oid, "customer_name": name, "customer_email": email, "item": item,
         "amount": amount, "status": status, "order_date": date}
    d.update(extra)
    return d

def task(tid, desc, turns, orders, checks, faults=(), heldout=False):
    t = {"id": tid, "description": desc, "turns": turns,
         "store": {"orders": {x["order_id"]: x for x in orders}},
         "faults": list(faults), "checks": checks}
    d = root / "evals" / ("heldout" if heldout else "")
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (d / f"{tid}.json").write_text(json.dumps(t, indent=2) + "\n")

from refunddesk.faults import FaultPlan


def test_explicit_calls():
    plan = FaultPlan.from_task("t", 0, [{"tool": "x", "kind": "timeout", "calls": [2]}])
    assert [plan.next_fault("x") for _ in range(3)] == [None, "timeout", None]

    rules = [{"tool": "x", "kind": "timeout", "rate": 0.5, "max": 2}]
    runs = []
    for _ in range(2):
        plan = FaultPlan.from_task("task", 7, rules)
        runs.append([plan.next_fault("x") for _ in range(20)])

        patterns.add(tuple(plan.next_fault("x") for _ in range(6)))

    validate_tool_result,
)

    "raw",
    [
        '{"order_id": "A1", "order_id": "A2"}',

        '{"order_id": "A1", "extra": 1}',

        '["A1"]',
        "not json",
    ],
)
def test_strict_argument_parsing_rejects(raw):

def test_strict_parsing_rejects_nan_and_bool_amounts():
    with pytest.raises(ToolArgumentError):
        parse_tool_arguments(call("issue_refund", '{"order_id": "A1", "amount": NaN, "reason": "r"}'))
    with pytest.raises(ToolArgumentError):
        parse_tool_arguments(call("issue_refund", {"order_id": "A1", "amount": True, "reason": "r"}))
    with pytest.raises(ToolArgumentError):
        parse_tool_arguments(call("nope", {}))

    assert parse_tool_arguments(call("issue_refund", {"order_id": "A1", "amount": 5, "reason": "r"}))["amount"] == 5
    assert parse_tool_arguments(call("get_refund_policy", "")) == {}

    assert validate_tool_result("lookup_order", {"status": "failed"})[:2] == (False, True)
    assert validate_tool_result("lookup_order", {"status": "not_found"})[:2] == (True, False)
    assert validate_tool_result("lookup_order", {"status": "ok", "order": {"order_id": "A"}})[:2] == (False, True)
    assert validate_tool_result("lookup_order", "garbage")[:2] == (False, True)
    good = {"status": "ok", "order": {"order_id": "A", "amount": 1.0, "status": "delivered"}}
    assert validate_tool_result("lookup_order", good)[0]

    rt = make_runtime(faults=[{"tool": "lookup_order", "kind": "timeout", "calls": [1, 2, 3]}])
    agent = RefundDeskAgent(llm=scripted([]))
    assert agent._run_tool_call(call("lookup_order", {"order_id": "A1"}))["status"] == "ok"
    assert [e["outcome"] for e in rt.log] == ["timeout"] * 3 + ["ok"]
    assert "A1" in agent.verified_orders

    assert "A1" in agent.failed_lookups

    assert "lookup failed" in blocked["error"]
    assert rt.store.load()["refunds"] == []

    agent = RefundDeskAgent(llm=scripted([]))

    result = agent._run_tool_call(call("issue_refund", {"order_id": "BIG", "amount": 900, "reason": "r"}))
    assert "must be escalated" in result["error"]

        {"role": "assistant", "content": "a"},

        {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": []},
        {"role": "tool_results", "results": []},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": "b"},

"""Run the eval suite: ``python -m refunddesk.suite --reps 3``.

Each (task, repetition) runs ``python -m refunddesk.eval`` in its own process,
exactly as a test harness would, with CULPRIT_RUN_ID / COMMIT_SHA / TASK_ID /
REPETITION set in the environment. Results go to a JSONL file and a summary is
printed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from .config import PROJECT_ROOT
from .tasks import list_tasks


def _git_head() -> str:
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.strip() or "unknown"


def _run_one(task_id: str, rep: int, seed: int, run_id: str, commit: str) -> dict:
    env = dict(os.environ, CULPRIT_RUN_ID=run_id, COMMIT_SHA=commit, TASK_ID=task_id, REPETITION=str(rep))
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "refunddesk.eval", "--task", task_id, "--seed", str(seed)],
        cwd=PROJECT_ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    try:
        result = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    except (IndexError, ValueError):
        result = {"task_id": task_id, "passed": False, "error": f"no JSON output; stderr: {proc.stderr[-500:]}"}
    result["repetition"] = rep
    return result


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m refunddesk.suite", description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--no-heldout", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--task", action="append", help="limit to these task ids (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    tasks = [t for t in list_tasks(include_heldout=not args.no_heldout) if not args.task or t.id in args.task]
    run_id = args.run_id or f"suite-{time.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}"
    commit = os.environ.get("COMMIT_SHA") or _git_head()
    out = args.out or PROJECT_ROOT / ".cache" / "refunddesk" / "runs" / f"{run_id}.jsonl"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    jobs = [(t.id, rep) for rep in range(1, args.reps + 1) for t in tasks]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
        results = list(pool.map(lambda j: _run_one(j[0], j[1], args.seed, run_id, commit), jobs))
    with out.open("w") as fh:
        for r in results:
            fh.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")

    print(f"run_id={run_id} commit={commit} results={out}")
    for rep in range(1, args.reps + 1):
        rows = [r for r in results if r["repetition"] == rep]
        passed = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("passed"))
        print(f"repetition {rep}: {passed}/{len(rows)} passed")
    failures = [r for r in results if not r.get("passed")]
    for r in failures:
        failed_checks = [c["detail"] for c in r.get("checks", []) if not c["passed"]]
        print(f"FAIL {r['task_id']} rep={r['repetition']} trace={r.get('trace_id')} {failed_checks or r.get('error')}")
    total_cost = sum(r.get("cost") or 0 for r in results)
    print(f"total: {len(results) - len(failures)}/{len(results)} passed, cost ${total_cost:.4f}")
    return 0 if not failures else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

input.content:
"""Verify persisted neatlogs traces for RefundDesk eval runs.

Usage:
    uv run python -m refunddesk.eval --task refund_small_order --seed 1 > run.json
    uv run python scripts/neatlogs_readback.py run.json [more.jsonl ...]

Input is the JSON printed by the eval runner (one object per line). For each run
the script reads the trace back through the neatlogs CLI (`neatlogs traces get`,
`traces spans list`, `traces raw-spans`, `traces payload`) and checks:

* the trace is finalized and carries the run metadata as tags;
* exactly one root (WORKFLOW ``refunddesk.run_task``), one AGENT span per turn;
* every LLM request and every mock tool execution is a span whose parent is an
  AGENT span under that root, in both the raw and the canonical projections;
* span counts match what the application executed (including failed requests
  and timed-out tool attempts, which must be ERROR spans);
* the root payload contains the same metadata.

Credentials: readback uses the CLI's saved OAuth login, or NEATLOGS_TOKEN when
set. The application's ingest key (NEATLOGS_API_KEY) is removed from the CLI's
environment because the CLI would otherwise treat it as a read credential.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

MAX_PAGES = 20
FINALIZE_POLLS = 12
POLL_SECONDS = 5


def _cli_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", None)  # ingest key: never a read credential here
    return env


def cli(*args: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    proc = subprocess.run(["neatlogs", *args, "--json"], env=_cli_env(), capture_output=True, text=True)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"neatlogs {' '.join(args)} failed ({proc.returncode}): {proc.stdout[-300:]} {proc.stderr[-300:]}")
    return json.loads(proc.stdout)


def paged(*args: str) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], bool]:
    """Collect every page; returns (items, complete)."""
    items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    cursor = None
    for _ in range(MAX_PAGES):
        extra = ["--cursor", cursor] if cursor else []
        data = cli(*args, "--limit", "50", *extra)["data"]
        items += data["spans"]
        cursor = data["page"]["nextCursor"]
        if not cursor:
            return items, True
    return items, False


def wait_finalized(trace_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    last: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for _ in range(FINALIZE_POLLS):
        try:
            last = cli("traces", "get", trace_id)["data"]
        except RuntimeError as exc:  # not ingested yet
            last = {"error": str(exc)}
        if last.get("finalizationStatus") in ("finalized", "dlq"):
            return last
        time.sleep(POLL_SECONDS)
    return last


def verify(run: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    trace_id = run["trace_id"]
    meta = run["metadata"]
    checks: list[tuple[str, bool, str]] = []

    def check(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
        checks.append((name, bool(ok), detail))

    trace = wait_finalized(trace_id)
    check("finalized", trace.get("finalizationStatus") == "finalized", str(trace.get("finalizationStatus")))
    if trace.get("finalizationStatus") != "finalized":
        return {"trace_id": trace_id, "task_id": run.get("task_id"), "passed": False,
                "checks": [{"check": n, "passed": ok, "detail": d} for n, ok, d in checks]}
    check("workflow_name", trace["workflowName"] == "refunddesk-eval", trace["workflowName"])
    check("trace_name", trace["traceName"] == "refunddesk.run_task", str(trace["traceName"]))
    tags = set(trace.get("tags") or [])
    for key in ("culprit_run_id", "commit_sha", "task_id", "repetition"):
        check(f"tag:{key}", f"{key}:{meta[key]}" in tags, f"{key}:{meta[key]}")

    raw, raw_complete = paged("traces", "raw-spans", trace_id)
    canon, canon_complete = paged("traces", "spans", "list", trace_id)
    check("pagination_complete", raw_complete and canon_complete, f"raw={len(raw)} canonical={len(canon)}")
    check("span_count_matches_summary", len(canon) == trace["spansCount"], f"{len(canon)} vs {trace['spansCount']}")

    for label, spans in (("raw", raw), ("canonical", canon)):
        by_id = {s["spanId"]: s for s in spans}
        roots = [s for s in spans if not s["parentSpanId"]]
        check(f"{label}:single_root", len(roots) == 1 and roots[0]["spanType"] == "WORKFLOW",
              f"{[(r['spanType'], r['spanName']) for r in roots]}")
        root_id = roots[0]["spanId"] if roots else None
        agents = [s for s in spans if s["spanType"] == "AGENT"]
        check(f"{label}:agent_per_turn", len(agents) == run["turns"]
              and all(a["parentSpanId"] == root_id for a in agents), f"{len(agents)} AGENT spans, {run['turns']} turns")
        agent_ids = {a["spanId"] for a in agents}
        llm = [s for s in spans if s["spanType"] == "LLM"]
        tool = [s for s in spans if s["spanType"] == "TOOL"]
        check(f"{label}:llm_spans_parented", all(s["parentSpanId"] in agent_ids for s in llm),
              f"{len(llm)} LLM spans")
        check(f"{label}:tool_spans_parented", all(s["parentSpanId"] in agent_ids for s in tool),
              f"{len(tool)} TOOL spans")
        check(f"{label}:no_dangling_parents",
              all(s["parentSpanId"] in by_id for s in spans if s["parentSpanId"]), "")
        check(f"{label}:llm_count", len(llm) == run["llm_requests"], f"{len(llm)} spans vs {run['llm_requests']} requests")
        check(f"{label}:tool_count", len(tool) == run["tool_executions"],
              f"{len(tool)} spans vs {run['tool_executions']} executions")
        llm_errors = sum(1 for s in llm if s["status"] == "ERROR")
        check(f"{label}:llm_error_spans", llm_errors == run["llm_requests"] - run["llm_calls"],

# RefundDesk

RefundDesk is a small customer-support agent for refund requests, built for neatHack.
It uses mock order and refund tools, has a deterministic eval suite, and traces every run with neatlogs.
See `hackathon.md` for the build log.

## Setup

```bash
uv sync                     # Python 3.12, locked dependencies (uv.lock)
cp .env.example .env        # then fill in the keys
```

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `LLM_PROVIDER` | `anthropic` (default) or `openrouter` (OpenAI-compatible, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`) |
| `VICTIM_MODEL` | Model id the agent uses (required; never hardcoded) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | Provider credential |
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | neatlogs **project ingest** key, used by the app to export traces |
| `CULPRIT_RUN_ID`, `COMMIT_SHA`, `TASK_ID`, `REPETITION` | Set by the test harness and attached to every trace (local fallbacks are marked `fallback` in the trace metadata) |

The agent requests temperature 0. Some Anthropic models reject sampling parameters with
HTTP 400 (`claude-sonnet-5-5` does). In that case `llm.py` retries without `temperature`
and caches that decision in `.cache/refunddesk/sampling.json`. The eval output reports
`temperature_sent`.

## Layout

- `src/refunddesk/llm.py` is the only module that talks to a model provider.
- `src/refunddesk/agent.py` holds the agent loop. It has the system prompt with the business rules, strict tool-argument parsing, validation of every tool result, retries (`MAX_RETRIES = 3`) and a history window.
- `src/refunddesk/tools.py` has the mock tools over a local JSON store (`store.py`), with deterministic fault injection from `faults.py`.
- `evals/*.json` holds 20 tasks and `evals/heldout/*.json` holds 6 more. Each task has turns, an initial store, faults and deterministic checks (`checks.py`).

## Running

```bash
uv run python -m refunddesk.eval --task refund_small_order --seed 1   # one task, prints JSON
uv run python -m refunddesk.suite --reps 3                             # whole suite, 3 repetitions
uv run pytest                                                          # unit tests (no network)
```

`refunddesk.eval` prints one JSON object with these fields:

- `passed`, `cost` (USD), `latency` (s), `tokens`, `trace_id`
- `checks`, `metadata`
- `llm_calls`, `llm_requests`, `tool_executions`, `tool_outcomes`

## neatlogs tracing

One eval run is one neatlogs trace in workflow `refunddesk-eval`:

```
WORKFLOW refunddesk.run_task            root; tags + neatlogs.metadata carry the run metadata
└─ AGENT refunddesk.handle_turn         one per customer turn
   ├─ LLM anthropic.messages.create     one per provider request (neatlogs.wrap); rejected requests are ERROR spans
   └─ TOOL lookup_order / issue_refund / ...   one per tool execution attempt; injected timeouts are ERROR spans
```

The four harness variables are attached as trace tags (`culprit_run_id:…`, `commit_sha:…`,
`task_id:…`, `repetition:…`), as `neatlogs.metadata` / `neatlogs.workflow.*` attributes on
the root span, and in the root span's input payload.

### Reading traces back (verification loop)

Readback uses the neatlogs **Public CLI** (`npm i -g neatlogs-cli`), not the ingest key:

```bash
neatlogs profile set work --host https://app.neatlogs.com
neatlogs profile use work
env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY -u NEATLOGS_TOKEN neatlogs auth login --device   # approve in browser
env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY -u NEATLOGS_TOKEN neatlogs whoami --json         # actor + project id
```

Credential isolation:

- The CLI treats `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` as a legacy read credential, so always strip it from the readback process.
- For saved OAuth access, strip `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` as well.
- For unattended runs, use a project-bound service-account token in `NEATLOGS_TOKEN`.

In a `uv run` shell, `.venv/bin/neatlogs` is the Python SDK's Doctor executable, not the Public CLI.
The verifier resolves the Public CLI explicitly; set `NEATLOGS_CLI=/path/to/neatlogs` to override it.

Run a fresh, correlated execution and verify it:

```bash
CULPRIT_RUN_ID=check-$(date +%s) COMMIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) TASK_ID=refund_small_order REPETITION=1 \
  uv run python -m refunddesk.eval --task refund_small_order --seed 1 > run.json
uv run python scripts/neatlogs_readback.py run.json        # also accepts suite JSONL files
```

`scripts/neatlogs_readback.py` waits for the trace to be finalized. It then reads `traces get`, every page of
`traces spans list` and `traces raw-spans`, and the `traces payload` of the root, LLM and TOOL spans. It checks:

- the run metadata tags
- a single WORKFLOW root and one AGENT span per turn
- every LLM and TOOL span parented to an AGENT span, in both projections
- span counts equal to the LLM requests and tool executions the app made, with failures as ERROR spans
- every executed tool call matching a `tool_use` request from the model
- the run metadata in the root payload

Manual commands it uses:

```bash
NL="env -u NEATLOGS_API_KEY -u NEATLOGS_TOKEN neatlogs"
$NL traces list --workflow refunddesk-eval --limit 10 --json
$NL traces get <trace-id> --json
$NL traces spans list <trace-id> --limit 50 --json      # follow data.page.nextCursor with --cursor
$NL traces raw-spans <trace-id> --limit 50 --json
$NL traces payload <trace-id> <span-id> --fields input,output,error --json
```

Known limitation: the public payload API returns text input/output only. For an LLM span
whose response is only `tool_use` blocks, the output field is empty. The SDK records the
request as `neatlogs.llm.tool_calls.*` attributes, but the Public API doesn't expose arbitrary
attributes. The request is still visible in the next LLM span's input, which the verifier uses.

# neatHack build log — RefundDesk

## Project

- **Name:** RefundDesk
- **Purpose:** A small customer-support agent that handles refund requests with tools, business rules, and failure recovery, plus a deterministic eval suite.
- **Problem:** Support agents that issue refunds must follow policy (escalation thresholds, no refund on failed lookups) and recover from flaky tools. Regressions are hard to spot without traced, repeatable evals.

## Team

- Pending: the builder hasn't yet said which names or handles to publish.

## Stack

- Planned: Python 3.12, managed with `uv`.
- Planned: LLM via Anthropic (default) or OpenRouter, selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`.
- neatlogs: CLI 0.2.0 installed and `doctor --probe` passed before this log started. Planned use is SDK tracing of every eval run, with readback through the CLI.
- Entire: CLI 0.11.4, enabled with `entire enable --agent claude-code`. Used for session checkpoints on commits.
- cfo.ai: required by the hackathon for the business plan. Pending, not started.

## Build log

### 2026-10-10

- Setup: configured the neatlogs CLI profile `work` (host `https://app.neatlogs.com`) and started device login for readback.
- Saved the neatHack skill to `.claude/skills/neathack/SKILL.md` and created this log.

## Demo

- Pending: no demo URL or instructions yet.

## Known limitations and next steps

- Next: build the agent, mock tools, eval suite, and neatlogs tracing.
- Pending: cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway).

## Submission

Confirmed requirements, from https://neatlogs.com/hackathon (read 2026-10-10):

- The event runs October 10–12, 2026 (online). Hacking starts 12:30 PM IST on October 10.
- The submission window is Monday, October 12, 7:00–11:55 PM IST.
- Must use neatlogs and Entire to build and improve the agent, and cfo.ai to plan the business.
- Code must be written during the hackathon, in a public repo with commits dated during the event.
- Submit on X by quoting the official neatlogs post with team, name, project, public repo, and demo.
- Evidence to include:
  - Before-and-after runs with compared numbers
  - neatlogs traces or screenshots
  - Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output
  - cfo.ai business plan
  - A run where an action failed and the agent recovered
  - Public sharing tagged #neatHack

Outstanding:

- The submission post link isn't published yet ("Submissions opening soon").
- cfo.ai plan
- Demo video
- Building-in-public posts
- Team names

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("hackathon.md"); s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace('''- Planned: Python 3.12, managed with `uv`.
- Planned: LLM via Anthropic (default) or OpenRouter, selected by `LLM_PROVIDER`.
- neatlogs: CLI 0.2.0 installed and `doctor --probe` passed before this log started. Planned use is SDK tracing of every eval run, with readback through the CLI.''','''- Python 3.12, managed with `uv` (`uv.lock` committed).
- LLM: Anthropic Messages API (`anthropic` 1.13.0) by default. The model is set by `VICTIM_MODEL`; runs so far used `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
  OpenRouter (OpenAI-compatible) is implemented but **not yet run**, because no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is configured.
- neatlogs:
  - The Python SDK (`neatlogs` 1.4.26) traces every eval run: WORKFLOW → AGENT → LLM/TOOL spans.
  - The Public CLI (`neatlogs-cli` 0.2.0) reads traces back to verify them (`scripts/neatlogs_readback.py`).''')
s=s.replace('''- Setup: configured the neatlogs CLI profile `work` (host `https://app.neatlogs.com`) and started device login for readback.
- Saved the neatHack skill to `.claude/skills/neathack/SKILL.md` and created this log.''','''- Setup: configured the neatlogs CLI profile `work` (host `https://app.neatlogs.com`) and signed in with device login.
  - The first device code expired: `{"code":"OAUTH_EXPIRED_TOKEN"}`.
  - The second approval worked (`whoami` OK), although the login process itself exited 8 with `{"code":"OAUTH_NETWORK_ERROR"}`.
- Saved the neatHack skill to `.claude/skills/neathack/SKILL.md` and created this log.
- Entire: checked that checkpoints are stored as `refs/entire/checkpoints/<xx>/<id>` refs, pushed to origin.
  - `entire checkpoint explain <sha> --json` works on a full SHA and its output parses as JSON.
  - A fresh clone fetches the checkpoint ref on demand.
- Built the agent (`src/refunddesk`), covering:
  - one model module (`llm.py`)
  - business rules in the system prompt and as code guards before `issue_refund`
  - strict tool-argument JSON parsing and validation of every tool result
  - `MAX_RETRIES = 3` and a history window
  - mock tools over a JSON store with seeded, deterministic fault injection
- Eval suite: 20 tasks in `evals/` and 6 held-out tasks in `evals/heldout/`, with deterministic checks on the final store and the tool-call log. Runner: `python -m refunddesk.eval --task <id> --seed <n>`.
- Finding: `claude-sonnet-5-5` rejects `temperature` with HTTP 400 ("`temperature` is deprecated for this model").
  The agent requests temperature 0, then on that 400 resends without it and caches the decision. Runs report `temperature_sent: false`.
- neatlogs integration:
  - SDK Doctor `--local` and `--probe` passed on SDK 1.4.26.
  - 9 evidence runs (success, multi-turn, timeout, persistent failure, LLM 400, 4 concurrent runs) all passed CLI readback: finalized, metadata tags, single root, every LLM/TOOL span parented to an AGENT span, exact span counts, and failures recorded as ERROR spans.
  - Fixed along the way:
    - SDK INFO log on stdout broke the runner's JSON output; fixed with `NEATLOGS_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING`.
    - Inside `uv run`, the SDK's `neatlogs` binary shadows the Public CLI; the verifier now resolves the CLI explicitly.
    - A transient CLI `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` aborted the verifier; it now retries with bounded backoff.
- Unit tests: 27 passing (no network).
- First full suite pass: 26/26. Baseline at `a89cc91`, 3 repetitions: 26/26, 26/26, 26/26 (78/78), $1.27 total by the agent's price table.''')
s=s.replace('''- Next: build the agent, mock tools, eval suite, and neatlogs tracing.
- Pending: cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway).''','''- The OpenRouter provider path hasn't been run (no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`).
- The neatlogs Public API payload shows no output text for LLM spans that return only `tool_use` blocks. Tool requests are verified through the next LLM span's input instead.
- Cost differs between sources: the runner's price table uses $2/$10 per MTok for `claude-sonnet-5-5`, but neatlogs reported $0.025422 for a run the runner priced at $0.016948.
- Pending: cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway).''')
p.write_text(s)
EOF
echo ok

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: build_hist.sh <branch> <base-ref> <edit> [<edit> ...]
# Applies each edit as one commit on <branch>, running the unit tests after each.
set -euo pipefail
REPO="/Users/rahilmavani/RAHIL MAVANI/Personal Projects/Hackathons/neathack/refunddesk"
SP="/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-rahilmavani-RAHIL-MAVANI-Personal-Projects-Hackathons-neathack-refunddesk/a82dfa19-aa1b-4afb-8e91-795d285f291c/scratchpad"
branch=$1; base=$2; shift 2
cd "$REPO"
if git rev-parse --verify -q "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null; then git checkout -q "$branch"; else git checkout -q -b "$branch" "$base"; fi
for e in "$@"; do
  msg=$(python3 "$SP/hist_edits.py" . "$e")
  # --frozen: run the tests against the locked environment without re-resolving pyproject
  if ! out=$(uv run --frozen pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1); then echo "TESTS FAILED after $e"; echo "$out" | tail -20; exit 1; fi
  git add -A
  git commit -q -m "$msg"
  n=$(git rev-list --count "$base..HEAD")
  echo "$branch #$n $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) $msg | $(echo "$out" | tail -1)"
done
